clue.text: Beetle has one motor at full speed

definitions.note: a beetle has a hard shell; 'one' stands in for the noun

parts.note: a motor is a car
apace means quickly, at speed

explanation.surface: A VW Beetle owner boasts their car has one engine flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' suggests the Volkswagen, and 'one motor' looks like a count; really 'Beetle has one' is the definition, the insect's hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard protective shell covering the back of a beetle or crab.

clue.text: Pigeon sound, quiet where pigeons live

parts.note: a pigeon's call is a coo
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A pigeon cooing softly in its loft.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a cage or pen for keeping poultry or pigeons.

clue.text: Hit by musician

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A chart hit performed by some musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' reads as a chart success but is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapper is a performer of rap music, so a kind of musician.

clue.text: Write article supporting new Ecstasy drug

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting part sits underneath, so the other letters come after

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to pen is to write
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a piece backing some fashionable new party drug.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts PEN and THE beneath N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthe is a legendary potion of forgetfulness in Greek myth, so a drug banishing grief.

clue.text: Female judge on stand employing name associate

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the stand word holds the name letter inside it

parts.note: to stand is to rise

explanation.surface: A woman judge in the witness box taking on a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand' suggests the witness box, but here it is the verb to get up; 'on' only joins the pieces in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To fraternise is to mix socially or be friendly with others, especially those one should keep apart from.

clue.text: Hospital department's purchasing Queen records

indicators.note: purchasing means taking in, so the department word holds the queen inside

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department, plus the 's
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An NHS department buys records of the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen records' looks like the rock band's albums; the Queen is ER and 'records' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to write them into a register, so enters means records.

clue.text: Prospect in waterway containing gold

indicators.note: containing means the waterway word holds the gold letters within it

parts.note: the Panama Canal is a famous waterway
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A view of a canal with gold in it, perhaps a prospector's hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospect' hints at gold prospecting but means a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view, and a prospect is an extensive view of landscape.

clue.text: In France the European capital turning shameless

indicators.note: turning means the combined letters are read the other way round

parts.note: la is French for the
Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A shameless European capital lurching about, seen from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral sense, so without shame about wrongdoing.

clue.text: Fish from Billingsgate perhaps going off?

indicators.note: Billingsgate fish market is in Cockney London, and Cockneys drop their initial aitches

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Is this fish from the London market going bad?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' suggests rotten fish, but it means straying; Billingsgate is London's fish market, where Cockney speech drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to stray from the right path, so erring is wandering off course.

clue.text: Theatrical group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: exaggerated and showy in style
second meaning: a faction sharing a view

explanation.definitionFit: Camp is both an adjective for affected, over-the-top behaviour and a noun for a body of supporters of one side.

clue.text: Nosed around, over cocky, having grounds?

indicators.note: around means the nosing word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to nose about is to pry, so nosed is pried
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
pert means cheeky or cocky

explanation.surface: A cocky busybody snooping, as if they had grounds to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having grounds' suggests having a reason; the question mark flags the sense of owning land.
explanation.definitionFit: Propertied means owning property, especially land and estates.

clue.text: Life line?

parts.note: not a rope thrown to save someone, but the line of work one follows through life

explanation.walkthrough: A lifeline is a rescue rope; split, it is one's line of work through life.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is the occupation a person pursues over their working life.

clue.text: Level match holding United finally

parts.note: even means level

indicators.note: holding means the match word grips the other letter inside it

parts.note: to tally is to match or correspond
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A drawn football game where United came through at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like an instruction to take a last letter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means in the end, after some delay, just as finally does.

clue.text: Embroiled in disaster is known star

indicators.note: embroiled in means caught up inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A celebrity star tangled up in a known catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped printing symbol, and printers call it a star.

clue.text: Good view from French tower, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the tower's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the Eiffel Tower in Paris

explanation.surface: The fine view one gets from the top of the Eiffel Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeful is a long good look at something, or a striking sight.

clue.text: Endless lunch as tea? It's indecent!

indicators.note: endless means the phrase loses its ends, leaving the inner stretch that spells the answer

explanation.surface: Outrage at serving tea in place of lunch, and at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the first letter of 'lunch' and the last of 'tea'; what remains, read straight through, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchaste means not sexually virtuous, so improper or indecent in conduct.

clue.text: Colour of cherry in seed, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means take the letters in the odd-numbered positions of these words

explanation.surface: Describing the shade of a cherry stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a deep reddish pink, from the French word for cherry.

clue.text: Service is, nevertheless, no good

parts.note: even so means nevertheless

explanation.surface: A grumble that some church service is no good after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in many cathedrals.

clue.text: Intellectual one in class

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the class word

parts.note: a genus is a class or kind in biology
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clever pupil, the brainy one in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is a person of exceptional intellect, so an intellectual.

clue.text: Pawn, possibly a piece

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
a is an example of an article in grammar

explanation.surface: A chess pawn might be considered one of the pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a chessman beside 'Pawn', but it means a fragment; 'a' is a grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny bit or fragment of something.

clue.text: Topping on minute unfinished tart

parts.note: topping is old slang for excellent, as is ace

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a tick is a moment or minute

explanation.surface: A tart with its topping put on in a minute, not quite done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' and 'tart' suggest baking; topping is dated British slang for excellent, and tart is sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic means of or like vinegar, so sour or sharp-tasting.

clue.text: Producer of empty beer vessel? No!

definitions.text: Producer of empty beer vessel? No!

indicators.note: empty means remove the inside, keeping only the outside letters

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Does a brewery make empty beer jugs? No, it makes the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole clue read straight: not a maker of empty beer jugs but of beer, which the 'No!' corrects.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer is someone who makes beer, the reverse of a maker of empty vessels.

clue.text: Wind up supporting British sausage

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: to wind someone up is to annoy them, to anger

explanation.surface: Teasing someone by backing the British sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a sausage, from the way it can burst when fried.

clue.text: Monkeys about with allowance for divorce

indicators.note: about means the monkey word is jumbled round

parts.note: apes are monkeys, loosely
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Monkey business plus maintenance payments: a messy divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly apes are not monkeys, but crosswords treat the two loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A separation is a formal parting of a married couple, short of or leading to divorce.

clue.text: Sweetheart trapping small bug

indicators.note: trapping means the endearment word closes around the other letter

parts.note: pet is a term of endearment

explanation.surface: A sweetheart catching a little insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying insect or creature, and a bug is the same.

clue.text: Peel and remove exterior, initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Instructions for peeling: start by taking the skin off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to cut away the outer skin of fruit or vegetables.

clue.text: For accommodation, send the invoice, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: to invoice something is to bill it

explanation.surface: An office instruction to bill someone for their lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging assigned to soldiers in a private house, so accommodation.

clue.text: Sportsman's first sporting, using bad language

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the sportsman word

parts.note: sporting a badge means wearing it

explanation.surface: A sportsman being first to swear on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' suggests sport, but it means wearing, as in sporting a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing is using profanity or obscene words, which is bad language.
